logp.method_description: The octanol-water partition coefficient (LogP) was determined based on Baron et al. (2014) using the shake-flask method. Stock solutions of the compounds were prepared in PBS buffer (Dulbecco's phosphate-buffered saline) and n-octanol in a 1:1 (v:v) ratio at a concentration of 1 mM. The solutions were stirred for 24 h at room temperature and then equilibrated for an additional 24 h at room temperature. The concentrations of the complexes in the organic and aqueous phases were determined using a UV-VIS-NIR spectrometer (Perkin Elmer Lambda 950). LogP is defined as the logarithm of the ratio of the concentrations of the complex in the organic and aqueous phases: logP = log([Concentration]octanol / [Concentration]PBS) or equivalently logP = log((OD)octanol / (OD)PBS)
